extraction.name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
extraction.description: VoiceAssistant-Eval is a comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. It comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories, including natural sounds, music, and spoken dialogue for listening; multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, and various scenarios for speaking; and highly heterogeneous images for viewing. The benchmark addresses four key weaknesses in existing benchmarks: lack of voice personalization evaluation, limited focus on hands-free interaction, neglect of various audio contexts in daily life, and insufficient multi-modal (vision+audio) integration assessment.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li (CUHK MMLab, SenseTime Research, CPII under InnoHK)
extraction.citeAs: Wang, K., Ren, H., Lu, Z., Zhan, M., & Li, H. (2025). VoiceAssistant-Eval: Benchmarking AI Assistants Across Listening, Speaking, and Viewing. arXiv:2509.22651.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from 47 source datasets spanning audio and visual modalities. For listening tasks, source data was extracted from 23 audio understanding datasets covering speech, sound, music, and general audio. For speaking tasks, data came from 22 datasets including 11 text datasets and 11 audio datasets, with role-play profiles from RoleBench. For viewing tasks, MMMU was used as the source dataset spanning 30 disciplines and 30 image formats. Text instructions were converted to audio using TTS models. 100 distinct roles were selected and three representative audio clips per role were collected for voice personalization tasks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Approximately 10% of candidate items were removed during curation due to missing or broken audio or images, ill-posed questions, or incorrect answers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data was extracted from 47 source datasets including: MMMU, VocalBench, AlpacaEval, MMSU, RoleBench, AdvBench, AIR-Bench, MEAD, BeaverTails-Eval, MT-Bench-101, VCTK, IFEval, MusicCaps, CommonVoice, SD-Eval, Nsynth, BIG-Bench Hard, Clotho, SLURP, VoiceBench, MTG-Jamendo, JL Corpus, MELD, AudioCaps, AudioGrounding, CoVoST 2, LibriSpeech, VocalSound, VoxCeleb1, MUSIA-AVQA, FoR, SpeechInstructBench, IEMOCAP, FollowBench, SpokenWOZ, TUT2017, AVQA, CommonsenseQA, GSM8K, STORAL, Clotho-AQA, FMA, CochlScene, Fisher, MT Bench, RAVDESS, MyST.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Text instructions were converted to audio using three TTS models (F5-TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B). Text preprocessing included: replacing image reference tokens with descriptive phrases, rewriting text using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct for TTS suitability (converting numbers, math expressions, and multiple-choice options to spoken form). Speech was evaluated with UTMOS Strong and regenerated until score surpassed 3.8. Synthesized audio was transcribed with Whisper-Large-v3 and the sample with the lowest word error rate was selected. In total, 13,471 high-quality speech audio files were synthesized.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A four-stage curation process was applied: (1) Deduplication using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance to flag potential duplicates, which were manually reviewed and removed, resulting in 15,359 samples; (2) Validation to exclude incomplete or unsuitable instances including entries with corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and demonstrably incorrect answers (approximately 10% discarded); (3) Categorization assigning remaining problems to 13 predefined task categories based on source metadata; (4) Sampling to balance the ratio of different tasks, resulting in 10,497 high-quality samples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Model responses were evaluated using a triadic evaluation system across three dimensions: (1) Content quality assessed using gpt-oss-20b with thirteen task-specific evaluator prompts; emotion evaluation used emotion2vec to get emotion probabilities; (2) Speech quality measured using UTMOS; (3) Consistency between text and speech computed using a modified Word Error Rate (WER) after transcribing speech outputs with Whisper-Large-v3. For role-play tasks, Wespeaker was used to calculate speaker similarity between model-generated speech and reference role audio. Human evaluation was conducted on 10% of Qwen2.5-Omni-7B responses (1,050 examples) across all 13 tasks for validation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A custom lightweight web-based curation tool was built for manual quality review. Automated evaluation used gpt-oss-20b, UTMOS, emotion2vec, Whisper-Large-v3, and Wespeaker.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation showed strong agreement with automated evaluation: overall Pearson correlation of 0.92 between gpt-oss-20b scores and human ratings, with agreement rate of 96.1%. Correlation coefficients ranged from 0.73 (robustness) to 1.00 (multiple categories). Evaluation stability was assessed by repeating scoring 10 times on 10% of samples, showing low variance (standard deviations mostly below 3). Statistical significance testing was performed using paired two-sided t-tests with Bonferroni correction.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: gpt-oss-20b (content quality evaluation), UTMOS Strong / UTMOS (speech quality evaluation), emotion2vec (emotion probability estimation), Whisper-Large-v3 (speech transcription), Wespeaker (speaker similarity for role-play tasks), F5-TTS / ChatTTS / Dia-1.6B (speech synthesis), Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (text rewriting for TTS)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and evaluation code will be publicly released under an MIT license. The authors bear all responsibility in case of violation of rights. A data governance process for auditing and removal is maintained, with the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes role-play voice imitation tasks involving speaker timbre and vocal characteristics. Five Chinese roles are included among 100 distinct roles. The dataset includes audio clips with speaker identity information (e.g., VoxCeleb1). The benchmark includes safety-sensitive content categories.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: VoiceAssistant-Eval is intended to push the boundaries of AI assistant capabilities and guide development of next-generation multimodal models. The benchmark addresses real-world applications in healthcare, education, smart homes, customer service, and automotive industry. The role-play voice imitation component raises concerns about identity spoofing, harassment, and fraud. The authors prohibit training or releasing models intended to reproduce identifiable speakers without documented consent, require downstream users to implement consent gating and watermarking, and provide safety cards describing acceptable use and known risks.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark is primarily in English, with only five Chinese roles in the role-play task, which may not capture the full variability of real user interactions. Questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources, which might not reflect the full richness or fairness concerns of real deployments. The role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles that may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas. Evaluation relies on GPT-based scoring which may favor certain phrasings or overlook nuanced errors.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset (10.5K items) may be limited in diversity. The monolingual (English) focus may not generalize to diverse linguistic settings. Only 21 open-source models and one proprietary model (GPT-4o-Audio) were evaluated. Automated evaluation with GPT-based scoring may introduce noise and bias. Video-audio integration and continuous audio-visual streaming tasks are beyond scope. The benchmark evaluates models in an offline, static manner and does not measure latency, partial utterance handling, barge-in, or error recovery. The benchmark is not intended for training models for cheating.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for Testing and Evaluation of voice AI assistants and multimodal models. Specific use cases include: evaluating listening ability (natural sounds, music, speech understanding), speaking ability (assistant tasks, emotion, instruction following, multi-round dialogue, reasoning, robustness, role-play, safety), and viewing ability (multi-discipline visual-audio integration). The benchmark is designed to facilitate research on personalized voice assistants, hands-free interaction systems, and multimodal AI systems.
